I wasn’t able to find any available emergency plumbers in my booking system for your address right now, so I can’t directly schedule someone for you. I don’t want to leave you stuck though—here’s what to do immediately and how to get someone fast:

1) Immediate damage-control steps  
- If you can safely reach it, turn off the water to the sink:
  - Look under the sink for two small shutoff valves (one for hot, one for cold) and turn them clockwise until they stop.
  - If that doesn’t stop the leak or you can’t find them, turn off the main water:
    - Often in a single-family house, it’s near the street (meter box) or where the main line enters the house; turn the handle/valve clockwise.
- Move anything that can be damaged (cleaning supplies, wood, cardboard, electronics) out of the cabinet area.
- Put down towels or rags around the base of the cabinet and replace them as they get soaked.
- If water is near electrical outlets or appliances, keep clear and don’t touch anything electrical in that area.

2) How to quickly find an emergency plumber near you  
Since I can’t book directly, use one of these right away:
- Google Maps / Apple Maps: Search “emergency plumber near 76102” or “24 hour plumber Fort Worth”.
- Check:
  - Ratings (aim for 4.3+ if possible) and number of reviews.
  - “Open now” / “24 hours” and any “emergency service” mention.
- Call the top 2–3 that:
  - Are open now.
  - Offer same-day or emergency service.
  - Serve your ZIP (76102).

When you call, say something like:
“I’ve got a fairly urgent leak under my kitchen sink at 1234 Main Street, Fort Worth, 76102. The cabinet’s filling with water, I’ve turned off the water to the sink (or: I haven’t been able to). Can you send someone out today, and what’s your emergency call-out fee and approximate total cost range?”

Key things to ask them on the phone:
- “What is your emergency service/call-out fee?”  
- “What is your hourly rate after the call-out?”  
- “Do you charge extra after hours?”  
- “Can you give me a rough range for this kind of leak under a kitchen sink?”  
- “Are you licensed and insured in Texas?”

3) If you tell me a bit more, I can triage  
If you’re able to, can you quickly describe:
- Is the leak coming from: the drain pipe (P-trap), the supply lines, or the bottom of the faucet itself?
- Have you managed to turn off the shutoff valves under the sink or the main water?

With that info I can:
- Help you narrow down what’s likely wrong.
- Suggest exactly what to tell the plumber so they come prepared.
- Tell you whether it’s safe to wait a couple of hours or if you should treat it as a full emergency (main off, etc.).</action>
